answer: Sybil defense runs on random peer audits. Each new agent is vouched for by a jury of existing identities drawn by lot, and jurors interact with it before granting one vote. Clones share behavior, so cross-checks eventually pair two of them and trace both to one operator, slashing the cluster. To forge control an attacker needs a long horizon of genuinely distinct human backers, each vetted independently, not mere keys. Hard-won trust, a pearl built slowly, is burned at the first caught fraud, so scaling the attack costs more than any gain.
